summary: Model version pin appears ignored when fallback routing activates (customer sees different model/version in response headers)
description:
Issue summary
Aurora Search reports that their pinned model version is being bypassed “randomly” and they are receiving responses from a different model version when capacity is constrained. They’re pinning a specific release tag but see a different version in response headers during periods of elevated latency.

Customer impact
- Perceived quality regression due to serving a different model build than the one they evaluated.
- Increased support load on their side (they are logging model/version headers for debugging and alerting).
- No full outage, but customer considers this a correctness/contract expectation issue (“pin means pin”).

Customer expectation
- If a request is pinned to an exact model version, Redwood should either:
  (a) serve that exact version, OR
  (b) fail clearly with an explicit error indicating pinned version unavailable.
- Customer does NOT expect fallback to override an exact pin without an explicit opt-in.

Environment
- Hosted API (self_serve)
- Regions observed: us-east primarily; one report in eu-west
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (streaming off)

What the customer is seeing
- Request uses a pinned model string, e.g. “redwood:llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2026-01-25”.
- During the problematic window, response headers/log annotations show:
  - x-redwood-model: redwood:llama-3.1-70b-instruct
  - x-redwood-model-version: 2026-02-06 (example)
  - x-redwood-routing: fallback_activated=true; fallback_reason=capacity
- They interpret this as “pin ignored.”

Requested from customer (per intake checklist)
- 3–5 request IDs that show mismatch
- Timestamp range + timezone
- Region
- Full response headers (or SDK debug logs) including x-request-id / x-redwood-* headers
- Confirmation whether they have any routing policy toggles enabled in Console (fallback/burst/region failover)

Initial triage notes
- This likely intersects with fallback routing policy behavior and/or how we surface model/version in headers.
- Potential failure modes:
  1) Customer has account-level fallback policy allowing cross-version fallback even when they pass a pinned model string.
  2) “Pinned model” is treated as a family pin (model family) not an exact build pin when the pinned build is unavailable in-region.
  3) Header reporting bug: request served from a compatible variant but the header shows a non-intuitive version tag.

Investigation plan / Support-safe checks
1) Confirm whether fallback activated for these request IDs using routing metrics:
   - Console → Observability → Routing → Fallback activations (by account, model, region)
   - Look for spikes aligned to timestamps.
2) Validate the customer’s account routing policy flags:
   - Console → Settings → Routing policy: “Allow fallback when pinned build unavailable” (if enabled)
   - Region failover (if enabled)
3) Confirm if the pinned build exists and is healthy in the reported region at that time.
4) If fallback is expected behavior, provide:
   - Clear explanation of “pin semantics” vs “fallback semantics”
   - Steps to disable fallback or enforce strict pin
   - Recommendation on pinned version strategy (move to latest stable, or use Dedicated if strict consistency required under load)

Escalation criteria
- Escalate to SRE/Platform Routing if we confirm:
  - fallback activated while strict pin enforcement is configured, OR
  - header/version reporting is incorrect or misleading in a way that impacts customers.

References
- Slack context: #eng-platform routing signals request (ref: sources/slack/eng-platform/1772029777.json)
- Workstream: ENG-4821 Add Support signal to routing fallback metrics (Support requested clearer confirmation fields)
comments:
2026-02-10 18:22Z — Priya Shah (Support)
Acknowledged. Asked customer for request IDs + timestamps + headers. Also asked them to confirm whether they enabled any routing policy toggles in Console (fallback/region failover). Noted that “x-redwood-routing: fallback_activated=true” suggests this may be expected behavior depending on policy. Linked intake checklist internally.

Next step: once request IDs received, validate via routing dashboards and confirm account policy flags.

2026-02-10 20:41Z — Customer (Aurora Search)
Provided 6 request IDs and a 45-minute window (approx 2026-02-10 16:50–17:35 PST). Observed in us-east. They confirmed they previously enabled “Allow fallback on capacity errors” after a separate incident and may have left it on. They still expect pin to be honored over fallback.

They attached excerpts showing x-redwood-routing fallback_activated=true and x-redwood-model-version values not matching their pinned tag.

2026-02-11 00:15Z — Mina Haddad (Platform / Routing)
Checked routing logs for 3 provided request IDs. Confirmed:
- Requests entered with an exact pinned tag.
- The pinned build was at capacity in us-east for that window and would have queued beyond the account’s configured max queue time.
- Account routing policy had “allow_fallback_when_constrained=true” enabled.
- Router selected a compatible build within the same model family (same architecture + safety profile), but not the exact build tag.

This is currently intended behavior when that policy is enabled; however, the UI language makes it easy to misunderstand “pinned model” semantics.

Action: propose adding a Support-facing signal that indicates whether fallback overrode an exact pin + the exact reason (capacity vs region failover). This is aligned with ENG-4821.

2026-02-11 17:05Z — Owen Phillips (Support incidents SME)
Drafted customer-facing explanation:
- Exact pin is honored unless fallback is explicitly permitted at the account/policy level.
- When fallback is permitted, Redwood prioritizes availability and will serve a compatible build if the pinned build is unavailable or would violate queue/latency guardrails.

Requested Docs/DevEx to review wording; suggested we add a short Troubleshooting entry: “Pinned model + fallback enabled = may receive compatible build; disable fallback to enforce strict pin.”

2026-02-12 19:22Z — Priya Shah (Support)
Sent customer the findings + steps:
1) To enforce strict pin: disable “Allow fallback on capacity errors” in Console routing policy (or set header/policy to require exact pinned build where supported).
2) If they want fallback but need consistency: pin to a “stable channel” (recommended) rather than a dated build tag; or consider Dedicated for guaranteed capacity.
3) How to confirm behavior: log x-redwood-routing and x-request-id; when fallback occurs, treat model-version as “served build,” not “requested build.”

Customer asked for confirmation that this will be documented and that fallback will never silently override a strict pin when fallback is disabled.

2026-02-13 18:10Z — Mina Haddad (Platform / Routing)
Confirmed: with fallback disabled, router will return an explicit error when the pinned build cannot be served (rather than selecting another build). There is still some ambiguity in how headers are presented; we should improve clarity. Tracking via ENG-4821 to make fallback signals easier for Support and customers to interpret.

No further engineering escalation needed unless we see fallback under strict mode (none observed in reviewed IDs).
resolution:
Root cause: Account-level routing policy allowed fallback under capacity constraints, which can override an exact pinned build selection to preserve availability/latency guardrails. The customer interpreted this as “pin ignored” based on served-model headers.

Mitigation provided:
- Customer instructed to disable fallback (strict pin) to ensure exact build is served or a clear error is returned.
- Customer instructed on how to interpret x-redwood-routing and model/version headers.

Follow-ups:
- Engineering: improve Support/customer-visible fallback signals in metrics (ENG-4821).
- Docs/DevEx: add a brief troubleshooting note clarifying pin vs fallback semantics (tracked informally via Support docs updates; no separate Jira created).

Customer confirmed resolution and will update their alerting to treat fallback as expected behavior only when fallback is enabled.
internal_notes:
Sensitivity: keep customer request IDs and exact timestamps out of broadly shared docs. If we publish pin/fallback semantics, do so generically.

If we see recurrence with fallback disabled, escalate immediately (potential correctness bug). In that case page Platform Routing + SRE per escalation playbook.
